children.name: animatableData
children.summary: The one property SwiftUI reads and writes while interpolating; map it onto whichever stored values should tween.

children.name: AnimatablePair<First, Second>
children.summary: Packs two vector values into one so a type with several animatable properties still exposes a single animatableData.

children.name: @Animatable macro
children.summary: On the version-26 OSes the macro synthesizes animatableData from every stored property, and @AnimatableIgnored excludes the ones that should not tween.

discussion: Animation works by interpolating animatableData between old and new values and re-rendering each frame. Custom shapes and modifiers adopt Animatable to make their numeric properties smoothly animatable; AnimatablePair combines multiple values.
name: Animatable
summary: Lets SwiftUI interpolate a type's data during animation.

children.name: body
children.summary: The scene list that becomes the app's windows, settings panes, and menu bar extras once the system launches it.

children.name: static main()
children.summary: The launch routine that @main invokes for you; calling it yourself from a main.swift lets a non-UI code path run first.

discussion: Marking a struct @main and conforming to App replaces the app delegate as the program's root: its body lists the scenes the app can present. App-wide state created here flows into every scene through the environment.
name: App
summary: The entry point declaring an app's scenes.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Receives each button's label and press state and returns the view that stands in for it.

children.name: ButtonStyleConfiguration
children.summary: The bundle handed to makeBody: the label view, the optional role, and whether a press is currently in flight.

children.name: ButtonStyle.borderedProminent
children.summary: System styles picked by static member — bordered, borderedProminent, borderless, plain — with no conformance to write.

children.name: ButtonStyle.glass
children.summary: The Liquid Glass styles of the version-26 OSes; glassProminent is the tinted, filled variant for the primary action.

discussion: Implement makeBody(configuration:) to restyle every button it is applied to: the configuration exposes the label, the role, and isPressed so the style can react to interaction. PrimitiveButtonStyle goes deeper and takes over triggering too.
name: ButtonStyle
summary: Custom button appearance driven by press state.

children.name: CommandMenu(_:content:)
children.summary: Adds a brand-new top-level menu whose items are ordinary buttons, toggles, and dividers.

children.name: CommandGroup(replacing:addition:)
children.summary: Swaps one of the standard groups — New, Save, Help, and so on — for the items you supply.

children.name: CommandGroup(after:addition:)
children.summary: Inserts items directly after (or, with before:, ahead of) a standard group while leaving that group intact.

discussion: Commands populate the macOS menu bar (and iPad key-command HUD) declaratively: group replacements, new menus, and keyboard shortcuts, attached to a scene with the commands modifier. This app adds its tab shortcuts this way.
name: Commands
summary: Declares menu bar commands for a scene.

children.name: animate(value:time:context:)
children.summary: Called every frame with the elapsed time; hand back the interpolated vector, or nil once the animation has finished.

children.name: velocity(value:time:context:)
children.summary: Reports the current rate of change so an animation that interrupts this one can inherit its momentum.

children.name: shouldMerge(previous:value:time:context:)
children.summary: Decides whether a new animation on the same value absorbs the one already running instead of stacking on top of it.

children.name: Animation(_:)
children.summary: Wraps a CustomAnimation conformer in the plain Animation type so withAnimation and the animation modifier accept it.

discussion: Added at WWDC '23, CustomAnimation exposes the animation engine itself: given elapsed time and a vector value, return the interpolated result — or nil to finish. Bounce, gravity, or any bespoke physics can drive standard SwiftUI animations this way.
name: CustomAnimation
summary: Defines your own timing curve or physics for animations.

discussion: Property wrappers conforming to DynamicProperty get an update() call before each body evaluation and may compose @State, @Environment, and friends inside — the machinery behind wrappers like @FetchRequest, and yours if you build one.
name: DynamicProperty
summary: Lets a custom property wrapper participate in updates.

discussion: An EnvironmentKey supplies a defaultValue, and an EnvironmentValues extension exposes it as a property. Since WWDC '24 the @Entry macro generates all of this from one line — reach for EnvironmentKey when supporting older targets.
name: EnvironmentKey
summary: The manual way to define an environment value.

children.name: effectValue(size:)
children.summary: Given the view's laid-out size, return the transform to apply when it is drawn.

children.code:
Text("Wrong password")
    .modifier(Shake(phase: attempts).ignoredByLayout())
    .animation(.default, value: attempts)
children.name: ignoredByLayout()
children.summary: Returns a variant of the effect that only touches rendering, so its animation frames never trigger a layout pass.

children.name: ProjectionTransform
children.summary: The 3x3 matrix an effect returns; build it from a CGAffineTransform, or from a CATransform3D when you need perspective.

discussion: GeometryEffect returns a ProjectionTransform for a given size and animates via animatableData — the home of shake effects and skews. Layout is untouched; only rendering transforms.
name: GeometryEffect
summary: An animatable transform applied to a view's geometry.

children.code:
DragGesture()
    .onChanged { value in
        offset = value.translation
    }
children.name: onChanged(_:)
children.summary: Runs your closure with the latest value as the gesture progresses; available when the value type is Equatable.

children.name: onEnded(_:)
children.summary: Fires once with the final value when the gesture completes, which is where commit-or-cancel decisions belong.

children.name: updating(_:body:)
children.summary: Writes transient state into a @GestureState that SwiftUI resets automatically when the gesture ends or is cancelled.

children.name: sequenced(before:)
children.summary: Chains two gestures so the second only begins after the first succeeds, yielding a two-case value to inspect.

discussion: DragGesture, TapGesture, MagnifyGesture and friends all conform to Gesture, which is what lets them compose: simultaneously, sequenced, and exclusively build multi-touch interactions from small parts.
name: Gesture
summary: The protocol behind drags, taps, pinches, and combinations.

children.name: inset(by:)
children.summary: Return a copy of the shape shrunk inward by the given amount; strokeBorder calls this with half the line width.

children.code:
Circle()
    .strokeBorder(.tint, lineWidth: 6)
    .frame(width: 44, height: 44)   // all 6pt stay within the 44pt frame
children.name: strokeBorder(_:lineWidth:antialiased:)
children.summary: Strokes with a style and width while keeping the whole line inside the shape's frame instead of straddling its edge.

children.code:
RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
    .strokeBorder(.secondary, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2, dash: [6, 4]))
children.name: strokeBorder(_:style:antialiased:)
children.summary: The StrokeStyle overload, for dashed or capped borders that still stay within bounds.

discussion: strokeBorder keeps a stroke fully inside a shape's bounds by first insetting it — which requires the shape to implement inset(by:). All built-ins conform; custom shapes need it to avoid clipped borders.
name: InsettableShape
summary: A shape that can inset itself, enabling strokeBorder.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Compose the title and icon views however you like and return the result for every label using the style.

children.name: LabelStyleConfiguration
children.summary: Exposes the label's two halves, title and icon, as independent views you can modify or omit.

children.code:
Label("Favorites", systemImage: "heart")
    .labelStyle(.iconOnly)

Label("Favorites", systemImage: "heart")
    .labelStyle(.titleAndIcon)   // both, even where a toolbar would drop one
children.name: LabelStyle.iconOnly
children.summary: Built-in styles selected by static member: iconOnly, titleOnly, titleAndIcon, or automatic to let context decide.

discussion: LabelStyle receives the icon and title as separate views, free to rearrange — icon above title, trailing icons, or badge-style compositions — applied anywhere via labelStyle.
name: LabelStyle
summary: Custom arrangement of a label's icon and title.

children.name: makeCache(subviews:)
children.summary: Create per-layout scratch storage once; updateCache(_:subviews:) lets you refresh it when the children change.

children.name: spacing(subviews:cache:)
children.summary: Tells neighbouring views how much space this container prefers around itself, typically by merging its children's preferences.

children.name: explicitAlignment(of:in:proposal:subviews:cache:)
children.summary: Override where a named alignment guide falls on the container; returning nil keeps the default edge-based position.

children.name: static layoutProperties
children.summary: Declares traits of the container up front — currently its stack orientation, which spacers use to pick a direction.

discussion: Layout puts your code where HStack's is: report a size from sizeThatFits, then position children in placeSubviews using their proposals and priorities. Flow layouts and radial arrangements become first-class containers that animate like built-ins.
name: Layout
summary: A custom layout container with full placement control.

children.name: makeCoordinator()
children.summary: Builds the long-lived helper object that receives AppKit delegate callbacks and pushes them back into SwiftUI state.

children.name: sizeThatFits(_:nsView:context:)
children.summary: Answers SwiftUI's size proposal for the wrapped view yourself; return nil to fall back to intrinsic sizing.

children.name: dismantleNSView(_:coordinator:)
children.summary: Static teardown hook invoked before the AppKit view is discarded, for detaching delegates and stopping work.

children.name: Context
children.summary: The NSViewRepresentableContext passed to make and update: your coordinator, the current environment, and the active transaction.

discussion: Implement makeNSView and updateNSView to host any NSView, with a Coordinator bridging delegates back to SwiftUI. The escape hatch when macOS AppKit offers something SwiftUI doesn't yet.
name: NSViewRepresentable
summary: Wraps an AppKit view for use in SwiftUI.

children.name: reduce(value:nextValue:)
children.summary: Merges a sibling's value into the running result; the order of calls follows the view tree, so accumulate rather than overwrite.

children.name: onPreferenceChange(_:perform:)
children.summary: Lets an ancestor observe the reduced value and copy it into state whenever it changes.

children.code:
Text(item.name)
    .anchorPreference(key: SelectionKey.self, value: .bounds) { anchor in
        isSelected ? anchor : nil
    }
children.name: anchorPreference(key:value:transform:)
children.summary: Publishes a geometry anchor — bounds or a point — instead of raw numbers, so the reader can resolve it in its own space.

children.name: overlayPreferenceValue(_:_:)
children.summary: Draws an overlay built from the reduced preference, which is how a selection highlight follows a child's bounds.

discussion: Preferences flow opposite to the environment: children set values, a reduce function merges siblings, and ancestors read the result with onPreferenceChange. It's how navigation titles reach the bar — and how children report sizes to parents.
name: PreferenceKey
summary: Passes values up the view tree, child to ancestor.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Return the button's view and wire up whatever interaction should count as activating it.

children.name: PrimitiveButtonStyleConfiguration.trigger()
children.summary: Runs the button's action; nothing happens until your style calls it, so the gesture that fires it is entirely yours.

children.name: Button(_:) with a configuration
children.summary: Re-creates a standard button from the configuration inside makeBody, for styles that tweak rather than replace the built-in behavior.

discussion: Where ButtonStyle only redraws, PrimitiveButtonStyle receives the trigger itself — you decide what gesture invokes configuration.trigger(). This is how long-press-to-confirm or double-tap buttons are built.
name: PrimitiveButtonStyle
summary: A button style that also owns the trigger behavior.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Return the progress rendering; you may nest a ProgressView(configuration) to reuse the default bar inside custom chrome.

children.name: ProgressViewStyleConfiguration
children.summary: Carries fractionCompleted (nil while indeterminate) plus the label and currentValueLabel views the caller supplied.

children.code:
ProgressView("Downloading", value: bytes, total: expected)
    .progressViewStyle(.linear)

ProgressView()
    .progressViewStyle(.circular)
    .controlSize(.small)
children.name: ProgressViewStyle.circular
children.summary: The two system styles, circular and linear, chosen by static member and scaled with controlSize.

discussion: ProgressViewStyle reads the configuration's optional fractionCompleted (nil while indeterminate) and draws anything — rings, waves, battery bars. This app type-erases between the built-in linear and circular styles in its ProgressView demo.
name: ProgressViewStyle
summary: Custom progress rendering from fractionCompleted.

children.name: body
children.summary: Compose several scenes into one named unit so an App's body stays a short list.

children.name: commands(content:)
children.summary: Attaches menu bar commands to a scene; every Commands conformer and CommandGroup goes in here.

children.name: defaultSize(width:height:)
children.summary: Sets the size a window opens at the first time, before the user resizes it and the system starts remembering.

children.code:
Settings { SettingsView() }
    .windowResizability(.contentSize)   // window hugs the content's ideal size
children.name: windowResizability(_:)
children.summary: Controls whether users may resize a window freely or only within what its content declares.

discussion: Scenes sit between the App and its views: WindowGroup, Window, Settings, DocumentGroup, and MenuBarExtra all conform. The system owns their lifecycle; scenePhase reports whether a scene is active, inactive, or backgrounded.
name: Scene
summary: A root container the system manages — windows, settings, menus.

children.name: updateTarget(_:context:)
children.summary: Mutate the proposed resting rect before the deceleration begins; the context tells you where it started and how fast it was flung.

children.name: ScrollTarget
children.summary: The proposed destination: a rect in content coordinates plus an optional anchor saying which point of it should align.

children.name: ScrollTargetBehaviorContext
children.summary: Read-only facts about the gesture: original target, velocity, content and container sizes, and the axes being scrolled.

children.name: .viewAligned(limitBehavior:)
children.summary: The built-in view-snapping behavior with a cap on how far one swipe may travel — never, always, or by one item.

discussion: Adopt ScrollTargetBehavior to bend the end of a scroll gesture: updateTarget receives the proposed resting point and may move it — snap grids, magnetic sections, or paging variants beyond the built-ins.
name: ScrollTargetBehavior
summary: Custom rules for where scrolling comes to rest.

children.name: path(in:)
children.summary: The sole requirement: describe the outline inside whatever rectangle SwiftUI hands you.

children.name: sizeThatFits(_:)
children.summary: Lets a shape answer size proposals itself instead of always filling the space it is offered.

children.code:
Star()
    .fill(.orange.gradient, style: FillStyle(eoFill: true))
children.name: fill(_:style:)
children.summary: Paints the interior with any ShapeStyle; the FillStyle picks even-odd winding and antialiasing.

children.code:
Circle()
    .intersection(Rectangle().offset(x: 20))
    .fill(.blue)
children.name: intersection(_:eoFill:)
children.summary: Boolean geometry between shapes (iOS 17 / macOS 14) — alongside union, subtracting, and symmetricDifference — producing a new Shape.

discussion: A Shape converts any rectangle into a Path, which makes it resolution-independent and reusable at any size. Conformers get fill, stroke, trim, and clipping behavior for free; animate custom geometry via animatableData.
name: Shape
summary: A view defined purely by the path it draws in a rect.

children.name: resolve(in:)
children.summary: Turn the style into a concrete one for the given environment — the hook custom styles use to adapt to color scheme or tint.

children.code:
Rectangle()
    .fill(.tint.opacity(0.3))
    .overlay(Text("Draft").foregroundStyle(.primary.opacity(0.6)))
children.name: opacity(_:)
children.summary: Derives a translucent version of any style, not just colors, so gradients and materials fade the same way.

children.code:
Text("Embossed")
    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
    .foregroundStyle(.white.shadow(.inner(color: .black.opacity(0.5), radius: 2, y: 1)))
children.name: shadow(_:)
children.summary: Applies a drop or inner ShadowStyle to the paint itself, giving text and fills an embossed look without a view-level shadow.

children.code:
RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16)
    .fill(.image(Image("paper"), scale: 0.5))
children.name: image(_:sourceRect:scale:)
children.summary: Static factory for ImagePaint, which tiles an image as a fill or stroke.

code:
Circle().fill(.blue)                    // Color
Circle().fill(.blue.gradient)           // AnyGradient
Circle().fill(.ultraThinMaterial)       // Material
Circle().fill(.linearGradient(
    colors: [.red, .orange],
    startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
discussion: ShapeStyle unifies what fill, stroke, background, and foregroundStyle accept: Color, gradients, materials, hierarchical levels, and image paint all conform. Custom conformances can resolve differently per environment, like a color pair that adapts to dark mode.
name: ShapeStyle
summary: Anything that can paint content — colors, gradients, materials.

children.name: draw(layout:in:)
children.summary: Walk the layout's lines, runs, or run slices and draw each into the context, applying per-glyph effects as you go.

children.name: sizeThatFits(proposal:layout:)
children.summary: Override the measured size when your drawing needs more room than the typographic bounds.

children.name: displayPadding
children.summary: Extra insets the renderer may paint into without being clipped — for glows and shadows that spill past the text.

children.code:
Text("Hello, world")
    .font(.largeTitle)
    .textRenderer(Jitter())
children.name: .textRenderer(_:)
children.summary: The view modifier that installs a renderer on a Text (or a view containing Text).

discussion: TextRenderer (WWDC '24) hands you the resolved text layout and a GraphicsContext: draw runs and glyphs yourself for per-character animations and effects that were previously Core Text territory.
name: TextRenderer
summary: Takes over how Text draws, line by line, glyph by glyph.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Build the toggle's view around configuration.label and flip configuration.isOn from whatever gesture you choose.

children.name: ToggleStyleConfiguration.isMixed
children.summary: True when the toggle represents a group with differing states, so a custom style can draw the indeterminate look.

children.code:
Toggle("Bold", systemImage: "bold", isOn: $isBold)
    .toggleStyle(.button)

Toggle("Wi-Fi", isOn: $wifiEnabled)
    .toggleStyle(.switch)
children.name: ToggleStyle.button
children.summary: System styles by static member: switch, button, and on macOS checkbox; button renders like a Button whose selection tracks isOn.

discussion: ToggleStyle's makeBody receives the label and the isOn binding — draw anything that flips the binding and every Toggle using the style inherits the behavior. The demo's checkbox/switch/button variants are the built-in conformers.
name: ToggleStyle
summary: Custom rendering for toggles.

children.name: body
children.summary: The toolbar items this type contributes, written with the same builder a toolbar closure uses.

children.name: ToolbarItem(placement:content:)
children.summary: One item at a semantic placement; the system maps cancellationAction, confirmationAction, and friends to the right spot per platform.

children.name: ToolbarItemGroup(placement:content:)
children.summary: Several controls sharing one placement, kept together as a unit.

children.name: ToolbarSpacer(_:)
children.summary: New in the version-26 OSes: a fixed or flexible gap that splits neighbouring items into separate Liquid Glass groups.

discussion: Conforming to ToolbarContent lets you factor ToolbarItem declarations into named types shared across screens, keeping placements consistent — the toolbar counterpart of extracting a subview.
name: ToolbarContent
summary: Builds reusable groups of toolbar items.

children.name: transferRepresentation
children.summary: List representations from most to least faithful; receivers take the first one they understand.

children.name: DataRepresentation(contentType:exporting:importing:)
children.summary: Serializes to and from raw Data under a UTType, with async throwing closures for each direction.

children.name: FileRepresentation(contentType:exporting:importing:)
children.summary: Transfers via a file on disk, the right choice for movies and other payloads too large to hold in memory.

children.name: ProxyRepresentation(exporting:importing:)
children.summary: Delegates to another Transferable type — often String or URL — so your type piggybacks on its representations.

discussion: Transferable centralizes serialization for sharing, drag and drop, and the pasteboard: describe your representations — Codable, data, file, or proxy — once, and every transfer surface understands the type.
name: Transferable
summary: Declares how a type moves via drag, copy, or share.

children.name: TransitionPhase
children.summary: Which end of the transition is being rendered; isIdentity marks the settled state and value runs from -1 through 0 to 1.

children.name: static properties
children.summary: Declares whether the transition moves content, letting the system substitute a calmer one when Reduce Motion is on.

children.code:
Text("Saved")
    .transition(Twirl().combined(with: .opacity))
children.name: combined(with:)
children.summary: Layers another transition on top so both run together.

children.code:
Text("Saved")
    .transition(.push(from: .bottom).animation(.bouncy))
children.name: animation(_:)
children.summary: Binds a specific animation to the transition so it no longer depends on the enclosing withAnimation.

discussion: The Transition protocol (2023) formalizes what AnyTransition compositions did: given content and a phase — willAppear, identity, didDisappear — return the modified view, and SwiftUI interpolates between phases.
name: Transition
summary: Defines custom insertion and removal animations.

children.name: makeCoordinator()
children.summary: Creates the object that adopts UIKit delegate protocols and forwards events back into SwiftUI.

children.name: sizeThatFits(_:uiView:context:)
children.summary: Respond to SwiftUI's size proposal directly, which fixes the common problem of UIKit views claiming the whole screen.

children.name: dismantleUIView(_:coordinator:)
children.summary: Static cleanup called before the UIKit view goes away — stop playback, remove observers, break delegate cycles.

children.name: Context
children.summary: The UIViewRepresentableContext with your coordinator, the SwiftUI environment, and the transaction driving this update.

discussion: The iOS twin of NSViewRepresentable: makeUIView creates the UIView once, updateUIView syncs SwiftUI state into it, and a Coordinator handles delegate callbacks. Prefer native SwiftUI when an equivalent exists.
name: UIViewRepresentable
summary: Wraps a UIKit view for use in SwiftUI.

discussion: A View is a lightweight value describing what to display; its single requirement is the body property. SwiftUI recreates these values freely and diffs them, so keep them cheap — state lives in property wrappers, not in the struct's stored properties.
name: View
summary: The requirement every piece of SwiftUI UI conforms to.

children.name: body(content:)
children.summary: Receives the view being modified as an opaque Content and returns the wrapped result; the modifier may own @State of its own.

children.name: View.modifier(_:)
children.summary: Applies a modifier instance to any view; a View extension usually wraps this call for a fluent name.

children.code:
let cardAndPulse = CardStyle().concat(Pulse())

Text("Hello").modifier(cardAndPulse)
children.name: concat(_:)
children.summary: Chains two modifiers into a single ModifiedContent value you can pass around and apply at once.

discussion: Conform to ViewModifier to bundle a set of modifiers — and any state they need — into one named unit, applied with the modifier function. Pair it with a View extension for a fluent call site.
name: ViewModifier
summary: A reusable transformation applied to any view.
